findings.description: make_home now scrubs only tokens.refresh_token before copying the host's ~/.codex/auth.json into the per-run HOME. tokens.access_token (a live ChatGPT/OpenAI bearer valid until exp, which the new pre-flight requires to outlive the whole batch, i.e. hours) and tokens.id_token (a JWT carrying the account holder's email/identity) are copied verbatim into /home/evaluser/.codex/auth.json, which is mounted rw into the container where the agent under evaluation runs with network access. The agent (driven by task fixtures and prompts that are evaluation inputs, not trusted code) can read and exfiltrate the operator's OpenAI credential; a0_bare arms that never run the dissent still receive the file.
findings.failure_mode: An agent run (or a malicious fixture/task that steers it) cats ~/.codex/auth.json and sends the access_token and id_token off-box; the operator's ChatGPT account is usable by a third party until the token expires, and the id_token leaks account identity. The KF-048 fix reduces blast radius (no refresh) but does not remove the long-lived bearer from the sandbox.
findings.suggested_fix: Only copy auth.json for arms whose plan actually runs the codex dissent (loa_mount true), and prefer a short-lived per-run token or a proxy that injects the bearer outside the agent-reachable filesystem. At minimum strip id_token (the CLI does not need it for API calls), mount .codex read-only for the agent user if the CLI tolerates it, and document that the access token is readable by the evaluated agent.

findings.description: remove_colliding builds `reserved` from the basename of every fixture .py under any directory component named tests/ or test/ (not just test_*.py collected by pytest), then unlinks any same-basename .py anywhere in the graded tree that is not a fixture or overlay path. Legitimate agent-added source modules are destroyed: a fixture tests/utils.py or tests/helpers.py causes an agent's new app/utils.py or pkg/helpers.py to be deleted before the hidden suite runs, so a correct solution is graded as failing with an ImportError. The deletion is silent to the agent (the sandbox is untouched) and only surfaces as a count in grade.json, so a graded regression would be attributed to the arm rather than the harness.
findings.failure_mode: Grading integrity: any agent that creates a non-test module whose basename happens to match a fixture helper module under tests/ loses that file in the grading copy and fails hidden tests it would otherwise pass; this biases ablation results between arms whose agents name files differently.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict both the reserved set and the removal walk to pytest-collectable test modules (basenames matching the suite's python_files pattern, default test_*.py / *_test.py) located under directories pytest will actually collect for the task's test_command, and never delete files outside tests/ or test/ directories. Log each removed path to the trial log as well as the sidecar file.

findings.description: `reserved` is seeded only from overlay entries that are files (`owned` excludes directory overlays). When a hidden overlay is a directory (tests/hidden/ containing test_a.py), its contained basenames are not reserved, so an agent-added tests/test_a.py is kept and the collection abort that 1.2.11 is meant to prevent still occurs for directory-shaped overlays.
findings.failure_mode: Tasks whose hidden suite is delivered as an overlay directory remain vulnerable to the import-file-mismatch abort, grading a correct solution as failing while grade.json reports colliding_tests_removed = 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Walk directory overlays (os.walk on f for isdir entries) and add their .py basenames to `reserved`, mirroring the fixture walk.

findings.description: spend_charge and budget_gate now take caller-supplied cap values (`cap`, `per`) and pass them straight to fadd/awk without the numeric check applied to `cost`. A non-numeric or empty value silently evaluates to 0 in awk, so an assumed-cap charge or the in-flight reservation becomes 0 and the --max-usd gate is bypassed for those trials. run-ablation.sh validates its caps with usd_ok today, but the library function is shared (run-arms and others) and the new parameters have no local guard.
findings.failure_mode: A future caller passing an unvalidated or empty cap disables the spend protection for failed/costless trials and in-flight reservations, allowing the batch to exceed --max-usd.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `cap`/`per` with the same regex used for `cost` (or usd_ok) and fall back to RUN_CAP with a logged warning when the value is malformed.
